newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche says Russia's London Club debt committed.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche says Russia's London Club debt committed.

text.p: Germany's Deutsche Bank AG said on Friday that virtally all of the Russian debt from the Soviet Union era eligible to participate in a rescheduling has been committed by creditors.
Deutsche, chair of the London Club of creditors, said reconciliation of the committed debt was underway.

Russia said in early September that commercial banks had agreed in principle to reschedule the debt, paving the way for a deal to reschedule all the $35 billion it owes to banks and for a long-awaited Eurobond issue.

Deutsche made the announcement after a meeting in Frankfurt between Russian Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov and Deutsche Bank official Christian Vontz, who chairs the London Club, ahead of IMF and World Bank meetings in Washington.
"Both stated that they are very gratified by the market's excellent reception of Russia's London club rescheduling," the bank, who is also the closing agent for the debt, said in a statement.
Russian officials have said the deal gives them approval to issue the country's first Eurobond issue and also a chance of getting an investment grade credit rating.

Kasyanov has said before that Russia planned to issue the Eurobond at the end of October or the start of November. Officials had earlier said that the Eurobond issue, worth $300 million to $500 million, would be issued in late September or early October.
U.S. ratings agencies have already been drawing up ratings for Russia, Kasyanov said.
